name: Proof that for any sum-free S, there exists A
notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

Proof that for any sum-free S, there exists A with |A|=c and A+A subset S^c

phase_0.boundary_condition: The additive group structure of the integers or finite cyclic group
phase_0.domain_name: Proof that for any sum-free S, there exists A
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: The forward shift of elements to find a candidate set A within the group

AREV.justification: The mapping back from the sumset A+A to the original elements to check for intersections with S

CLINK.justification: The sequential application of the probabilistic method to narrow the search space for A

ENGAGR.justification: The state where A+A and S share a boundary but remain disjoint in the limit

EVALF.justification: The detection of an element in A+A that exists within the sum-free set S

EVALT.justification: The confirmation that the intersection of A+A and S is empty

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the total group from the sumset and its complement to verify the subset relation

FSPLIT.justification: The division of the group into elements belonging to the sumset A+A and those that do not

IFIX.justification: The permanent fixation of the size of A as a constant c relative to the group size

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-consistency of set S remaining sum-free throughout the transformation

TANCH.justification: The final containment of the existence proof within the specified cardinality bounds

VINIT.justification: The state before any subset S is defined or the group structure is populated

phase_3.both_description: The probabilistic expectation where A+A is distributed across S and S^c before selection
phase_3.false_description: The condition where A+A contains at least one element of S
phase_3.true_description: The condition where A+A is contained within the complement of S
phase_3.void_description: The unindexed collection of integers before subset selection

steps.domain_action: define the group G and the sum-free subset S
verify S contains no x, y, z such that x + y = z
branch into candidate selection for set A
apply a random shift to the elements of G
compose the shifted elements into a candidate set A
fix the cardinality of A to the constant c
generate the sumset A+A from the candidate set
map A+A into the complement S^c
discard candidate A and re-index the shift
reconcile the sumset mapping with the group structure
merge the validated set A into the proof structure
hold the density of A against the sum-free constraint of S
record the existence of A as a permanent theorem
close the proof under the established cardinality

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The probabilistic method translating existence into a construction
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Additive group operations and set intersections
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The storage of the characteristic function of S
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The iterative search for a valid translation parameter

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational search through the translation space
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The proof organizes the group structure without adding information to the underlying axioms
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Verified existence of A satisfying the subset condition
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Unproven existence of A for a given S
